caseno: Criminal Appeal No. 8 of 1991 with Jail Petition No. 1 of 1991.
lawyer:
Korban Ali, Advocate, instructed by M Nowab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Appellant.
B Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
Abdul Quddus ----- Appellant
Vs.
The State ----- Respondent
case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 22.8.1990 passed by the High Court Division, Rangpur Session, in Death Reference No. 5 of 1988 and Criminal Appeal No. 178 of 1988)
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J: This appeal by condemned-appellant Abdul Quddus is directed against the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, Rangpur Sessions, Rangpur, affirming the Death Reference No. 5 of 1988, confirming the judgment and order passed by the Sessions Judge, Pabna convicting the appellant under section 302 of the Penal Code and sentencing him to death by hanging in Sessions Case No. 20 of 1987.

2. The prosecution case, in short, is that accused Abdul Quddus had land on the eastern side of the house of informant Dr. Mukbul Hossain. The accused grew IRRI paddy in that land and occasionally when he used to go there to give water in that land from his shallow tube-well he would take rest in the outer house of the informant. According to the informant, accused Abdul Quddus used to tease the informant's daughter deceased Hosne Ara @ Dilara and her younger sister Rousan Ara alias Mina while they used to go to school. Accused Abdul Quddus also sent a proposal for marriage with his daughter Dilara but the proposal was rejected by both Dilara and her parents. On 5.3.87 at about 6-45 PM while deceased Dilara and her younger sister Roushan Ara were reading in the southern room of the west bhiti dwelling but accused Abdul Quddus being armed with a dagger entered into that room through the eastern door. Seeing this both the sisters raised alarm and hurriedly went to the western room of south bhiti dwelling but and again from there crossed to the eastern room of the same dwelling hut. The accused chased them upto the eastern room and inflicted several dagger blows on the back of Dilara who after receiving those injuries, fell on a chouki and became senseless. Soon thereafter she was taken to Pabna Hospital where she succumbed to those injuries.

3. The appellant pleaded innocence and denied the occurrence. He further pleaded that deceased Hosne Ara @ Dilara was in love with him and that occasionally she used to go to the Shallow Machine room of the accused for which the parents of the deceased girl and her brother Matiaur Rahman abused her and assaulted her and in consequence of which she died.

4. In this case leave was granted to consider whether the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in upholding the conviction and sentence of the appellant on the basis of the evidence of only one eye-witness PW 2 Rowshan Ara @ Mina which was not corroborated and substantiated by any independent disinterested witness, that the High Court Division did not give sufficient importance to the evidence of the Medical Officer which was inconsistent with the oral evidence of this eye witness with regard to the alleged injuries caused by the appellant and that whether the facts and circumstances of the case calls for awarding the capital punishment.

5. In this case prosecution examined 17 witnesses and one witness was tendered for cross-examination by the defence. Defence did not examine any witness. The occurrence took place inside the dwelling but of the informant while deceased Dilara and her younger sister were reading in the southern room of the west bhakti dwelling hut. The accused entered into the reading room with a dagger in his hand chased her from one room to another and assaulted Dilara and in consequence of which she died soon thereafter. This occurrence of actual assault of deceased Dilara was seen by her younger sister PW 2 Most. Rowshan Ara @ Mina who was also reading along with the deceased in that room at the time of occurrence.On hearing the alarm of the deceased and her younger sister, PW 3 Most. Rabeya Khatun, the mother of the deceased and PW 4 Most. Kohinoor Begum, the Bhabi of the deceased rushed inside the room and saw the accused with a dagger in his hand. The other material witnesses namely PW 5 Dr. Matiar Rahman, the brother of the deceased, PW 6 Abdur Rahman and PW 10 Mahtab who used to reside in the outer house of the informant also saw the appellant Abdul Quddus going away from the place of occurrence with a blood-stained dagger in his hand.

6. Presently we will discuss the oral evidence on record in extenso to see whether the prosecution has been able to prove it's case against the condemned-appellant beyond the shadow of reasonable doubt.

7. In this case the First Information Report was lodged by Dr. Mukbul Hossain, the father of deceased Dilara after 75 minutes of the occurrence wherein he stated that at the time of occurrence he was not in his house. He lodged the First Information Report to the Officer-in-charge of Pabna Police Station who was present in his house after getting a telephone call that an incident has taken place in his village. The informant stated in the First Information Report that he heard about the occurrence from the inmates of his house that while his daughter deceased Dilara and his younger sister Rowshan Ara were reading inside the room accused Abdul Quddus entered into the room with a dagger and chased them upto the eastern room of the same dwelling but and the accused inflicted two serious injuries on the back side of Dilara by which she became unconscious and fell on a Chowki. The informant further stated that accused Quddus used to tease her daughter Dilara and gave proposal of marriage with her and the same was rejected by him and his daughter. As a motive of the murder it is stated that due to the refusal of the marriage proposal the accused with the intention of killing Dilara entered into the house on the day of occurrence and killed her. In his testimony before the Court he stated that his daughter deceased Dilara was a student of Class X of Tabunia High School and was aged about 17/18 years. He further stated that his house was fully electrified and all the rooms and corridors of the house were electrified. In cross-examination he stated that he heard that a telephone call was made to the Police Station but he could not say as to who made the call. He also stated that soon after the occurrence there were 30/35 people including PW 7 Md. Riazuddin Miah, PW 8 Dr. Habibur Rahman and others. He denied the defence suggestion that in consultation with his son this case has been falsely started against accused Abdul Quddus.

8. PW 2 Most. Rowshan Ara alias Mina is the solitary eye-witness in this case. She stated that she along with her sister Dilara were reading in the southern room of the west bhiti but and at that time accused Abdul Quddus entered the room through the eastern door with a big dagger in his hand and seeing this they were frightened and cried out. They escaped from that room and entered into the western room of south bhiti hut. Again from there the deceased went behind her to the eastern room of south bhiti but and the accused followed them upto that room. The northern door of that room was closed and while Dilara tried to open the door just at that time accused Abdul Quddus inflicted two dagger blows on the back side of her sister. On receiving the injuries she fell on the Chowki. She then started shouting and through the same door she tried to leave the room. Hearing her cries her mother PW 3 Rabeya Khatun, her Bhabi PW 4 Kohinoor Begum entered the room. She also stated that accused Quddus went away through the same door by which he entered into the dwelling hut. She further stated that there was electric light in every room and she could recognise accused Quddus clearly in the electric light which was burning in the room at that time. She also stated that soon after the occurrence she disclosed about the recognition of the accused to her mother, brother, Bhabi, father and to many other persons who were present after the occurrence. According to PW 2, Abdul Quddus was known earlier to her and he used to take rest in their outer house when he used to give water in his IRRI land from the Shallow Machine room. She also admitted that Abdul Quddus gave proposal of marriage with Dilara and the same was rejected by her sister, deceased Dilara, her parents and all of them. According to her, due to this grudge the accused killed her sister Dilara. She also stated that her brother PW 5 Matiar Rahman saw the accused going away from the place of occurrence with a dagger in his hand and her brother also fired a blank shot from his two-two-bore rifle. In her cross-examination she denied the defence suggestion that her sister deceased Dilara was in love with accused Quddus and she wanted to marry him and that Dilara used to go to the Shallow Machine room of the accused for which her parents used to rebuke her sister. She also denied the defence suggestion that she was deposing falsely at the instigation of her brother Matiar Rahman. From her cross-examination it appears that no vital contradiction could be elicited by the prosecution with regard to the factum of inflicting injuries by accused Abdus Quddul inside eastern room of the south bhiti but and of recognition of the accused at the time of occurrence. PW 2 was also mentioned as an eye-witness in the first information report. PW 3 Rabeya Khatun, the mother of deceased Dilara, was working in the kitchen at the time of occurrence along with her daughter-in-law PW 4 Kohinoor Begum. She stated that hearing hue and cry of her daughters she ran to their reading room and finding them not there she entered in the eastern room of south bhiti but and saw Abdul Quddus with a dagger in his hand and saw Dilara in a senseless condition with bleeding injuries on a chouki. She further stated that the accused was also assaulting her at that time and she caught hold of the left hand of accused. She also stated that she recognised the accused in the electric light. She also heard about the occurrence from PW 2 and saw the accused going away through the reading room of her daughter. She further stated that she disclosed about the occurrence and of recognition of the accused to her husband PW 1, son PW 5, PW 10 Mahtab and others. In her cross-examination she denied the defence suggestion that Dilara was in love with accused Quddus and that she did not see the accused at the place of occurrence. PW 4 Kohinoor Begum, daughter-in-law of the informant, stated that hearing hue and cry of deceased Dilara and Mina she along with her mother-in-law PW 3 went to the reading room of Dilara and found accused Quddus going away with a blood-stained dagger from the room. She could recognise the accused in the electric light and on entering into the eastern room of south bhiti but she saw Dilara lying senseless with bleeding injuries on the Chouki. At that time she also heard a sound of rifle shot and subsequently she learnt that her husband fired a blank shot from that gun. No material contradiction could be taken by the defence from her testimony. PW 5 Dr. Matiar Rahman, elder brother of deceased Dilara stated that while returning from Tabunia Bazar at a distance of about 100 yards from his house he heard hue and cry and rushed to his house and found Quddus coming out from the main door of the house with a blood-stained dagger in his hand. He could recognise the accused in the electric light and at that time darkness did not set in. He further stated that seeing the accused he was perplexed and on entering into the house he brought out two-two-bore rifle and fired a blank shot. At that time he heard cries of his mother, wife and sister and saw deceased Dilara lying senseless with bleeding injuries in the eastern room. He heard about the occurrence from inmates of the house, PW 9 Abdur Rahman and PW 10 Mahtab came soon thereafter. PW 8 Dr. Habibur Rahman and PW 7 Riazuddin also came to their house and they heard about their recognition of Quddus. According to this witness, Dilara died in the hospital. In cross-examination he could not specifically say as to who informed the police station but he admitted that someone must have given the information to the Police Station over telephone. In cross-examination he also denied about the love affair of his sister with Quddus. PW 6 Abdur Rahman was named as a witness in the First Information Report and this witness used to stay in the outer house of the informant and used to sell earthen potteries throughout the day as a hawker and in the night used to stay in the outer house of the informant. This witness hearing hue and cry inside the but came out and saw accused Quddus going out through the main gate with a blood-stained dagger in his hand. He also saw blood in the wearing apparels of the accused. He recognised the accused in the electric light of the house of the informant. He further stated that he also narrated about the recognition of Quddus by electric light to the informant. He denied the defence suggestion that he did not recognise the accused soon after the occurrence. PW 7 Md. Riazuddin Miah is a close neighbour of the informant living at a distance of 250 yds from the house of the informant. He testified that on hearing hue and cry from the house of the informant he went to the house of Dr. Mokbul Hossain and heard from PW 2 Mina, PW 3 Rabeya, PW 4 Kohinoor that accused Quddus assaulted Dilara with dagger and fled away. PW 8 Dr. Habibur Rahman stated that coming to the house of the informant he and others heard from the informant's wife and daughter that Quddus assaulted deceased Dilara and fled away. PW 9 Abdur Rahman, a seizure list witness stated that on 5.3.87 in the night he went to the house of informant and before him the police seized blood-stained earth, a blood-stained Chouki and a 60 watts bulb. PW 10 Mahtab is also an earthen pottery seller and used to live in the outer house of the informant. According to this witness, hearing hue and cry he went towards the house of the informant and saw accused Quddus, whom he used to know from before, going away with a blood-stained dagger in his hand. He testified that going inside the house he heard from the inmates of the house that Quddus fled away after assaulting deceased Dilara. He also narrated the occurrence to the informant after his arrival in the house from bazar. This witnesses was also named in the First Information Report. PW 11 Md. Abul Mohsin Khan, son-in-law of PW 1 is a witness to the inquest report. PW 12 Md. Humayun is another seizure list witness. PW 13 Sub-Inspector Kazi Anwarul Islam recorded the First Information Report. PW 14 Dr. Md. Shamsul Haque, the Resident Medical Officer of Pabna Sadar Hospital held post mortem examination on the dead body of deceased Dilara and found the following injuries:

"(1) One incised wound with marginal laceration extending from 2nd thoracic spine upto the anterior axillary fold at 9th intercostal space cutting muscles and the left scapula measuring 10 " x 5" x thoracic cavity deep.

(2) One incised wound measuring 4" x 2" x muscles deep at the mid point of the posterior surface of the left arm.

(3) One stabbing wound measuring 1-1/4" x x 2" on the back of the left lumbar region.

(4) One incised wound measuring 1-1/4" x 3/1" x skin deep on the left lumbar region at its lateral side.

(5) One incised wound measuring 1/4" x 1/4" x skin deep along the left mid axillary line just on the 7th intercostal space.

(6) One stabbing wound measuring 1/4" x 1/4" x left rectus muscles deep in the epigastric region.

9. On dissection antemortem blood and block clot present in and around the tissues of the injuries region (places)."

The Medical Officer in cross-examination stated that in postmortem examination report he noted that ribs No. 1, 3 and 4 found to be fractured through mistake but according to him actually ribs were cut. On re-call by the prosecution, the Doctor stated that injury No. 1 might be caused by heavy and big dagger.

10. PW 15 is a constable who was present at the time of inquest of the dead body of Dilara. PW 16 Ayub Ali was tendered by the prosecution and defence did not cross-examine him. PW 17 Md. Nurul Islam is the Chairman of Maligacha Union Parishad who testified that on the next day of occurrence in the evening he went to the house of the informant and heard about the occurrence from PWs 2 and 3 that on 5.3.87 at about 7-00 PM accused Quddus assaulted deceased Dilara with a dagger which caused her death. In cross-examination he stated that Dr. Mokbul Hossain is known to him and is also a friend of him. PW 18 Sub-Inspector Shamsul Hoque is the Investigating Officer who investigated into the case. He testified that on 5.3.87 he got a telephone call that there was a disturbance in Bagendrapur village under Babunia and on getting this information he went to the place of occurrence. According to this witness the OC of Pabna Police Station took oral FIR from the informant and according to the dictation of the Officer-in-charge, the FIR Ext. 1 was written down. The same was read over to the informant and who after having admitted its correctness signed the same. The Officer-in- Charge entrusted the investigation of this case to him on the spot. This police officer investigated into the case and thereafter submitted charge-sheet.

11. On a careful consideration of the entire evidence as narrated above, it appears that within 75 minutes of the occurrence the First Information Report was lodged and in that FIR the name of the accused Quddus was specifically mentioned as the assailant of deceased Dilara. Further, the name of all the material witnesses were mentioned in the First Information Report. Thus, the suggestion of the defence that the case was falsely concocted at the-instance of the brother of deceased Dilara cannot be accepted at all. Further, we have already indicated above that PW 2 in the facts and circumstances of the case being present inside the room where Dilara was murdered to death was the most probable and natural witness. As according to the prosecution, both the sisters were reading together inside the room the testimony of this solitary eye-witness PW 2 could not be shaken in any manner by the defence in cross-examination. We also find it very difficult to disbelieve her testimony as she narrated in details as to how accused Quddus entered into their reading room with a dagger in his hand and followed them through the other rooms of the dwelling but and ultimately assaulted in the eastern room of south bhiti hut. It is on record that hearing hue and cry of the deceased and PW 2, PW 3 mother and PW 4 sister-in-law entered into the room and saw the accused going away with a blood-stained dagger in his hand. It is also in evidence that PWs 5, 6 and 10 saw the accused going out of the house with a blood-stained dagger in his hand immediately after the occurrence. With regard to the recognition of this appellant there cannot be any doubt because all the witnesses testified that the house of the informant was fully electrified and they saw and recognisd the appellant in the electric light. Even it is on record that darkness was also not set in outside by the time the accused came out of the house of the informant. Broadly speaking the defence could not show any material contradictions and omissions in the testimony of PWs 2-6 and 10 for which we can disbelieve the prosecution case.

12. Mr. Korban Ali, learned Advocate, apart from placing the entire evidence on record, made his best efforts to point out the material discrepancies in the testimony of the prosecution witnesses.

13. He argued that PW 2 Most. Rowshan Ara, the only eye-witness in this case is only aged about 16 years and is a student of Class IX and as such she being an immature girl no reliance can be placed on her testimony.

<u>14. We have indicated earlier that she is the most natural, probable and competent witness in the present case as she was reading in the same room with her deceased sister Dilara and saw the entire occurrence. She has given details of the entire occurrence and even in her cross-examination the defence could not show any material discrepancy for which her ocular testimony should be disbelieved. She having deposed the entire incident from the beginning to the end it is very difficult for us to discard her evidence only on the ground that she was an interested witness and was a minor girl aged about 16 years. Even the law provides that a child witness can be relied if he/she is capable of under-standing and replying the question intelligently. Thus, this argument of Mr. Korban Ali is very difficult to accept.</u>

<u>15. The learned Advocate next contends that the oral evidence of PW 2 indicates that the deceased Dilara sustained two major injuries on her back. Whereas the medical officer found six injuries and as such according to him the four other injuries remained unexplained. We have already referred above to the injuries in details. From the testimony of the Medical Officer PW 14 Dr. Shamsul Haque we find that injury Nos. 1 and 2 are relatable to the oral evidence of PW 2. But the other 4 stabbing and incised wounds which were mentioned by the Medical Officer are of minor nature and are in the vicinity of injury Nos. 1 and 2 and we are of the view that even in the process of inflicting these two major injuries viz., 10" x 5" x thoracic cavity deep and another which is 4" x 2" x muscles deep; those other minor injuries could be caused. Further, these minor injuries which were only skin deep can be the result of involuntary movements of the deceased when the dagger blows were inflicted. Thus the ocular evidence of PW 2 with regard to injury Nos. 1 and 2 cannot be disbelieved. The ocular evidence of PW 2 was that accused inflicted two major injuries on the back side of Dilara while she attempted to open the eastern door to go out of the room. So it is quite likely that in this process these minor injuries might be caused as found by the Doctor. Hence, the four bleeding injuries being of minor nature it is not difficult to reconcile the existence of these four minor injuries on the person of the deceased as indicated by the Medical Officer. Thus, we cannot accept the argument of the learned Advocate for the condemned-prisoner that the only eye-witness should be disbelieved as there is some discrepancy with regard to these minor injuries as testified by her. It will not be out of place to mention that the medical evidence is only corroborative in nature. In that view, the ocular evidence of the eye-witness which substantially corroborates the major injuries on the person of the deceased must be accepted.</u>

<u>16. Mr. Korban Ali, learned Advocate, also wanted to argue that the deceased along with her sister were reading in southern room of the west bhakti but from where they crossed into western room of south bhiti but and ultimately went to eastern room of south bhiti where the occurrence took place and the prosecution story cannot be believed as the prosecution did not mention about the connecting doors in between these rooms. This argument is difficult to swallow, because PW 2 stated that through the reading room they went to the bed room of west bhiti but and from there they went to the east room, Thus, it is apparent that there was a connecting door in between these rooms. Further, if the defence was sure that there was no connecting door in between the rooms then it was for the defence to put this question in cross-examination to the prosecution witness. But there being no suggestion to this effect how can this ingenuous argument of the learned Advocate be accepted ?</u>

17. Lastly, coming to the question of sentence, Mr. Korban Ali submitted that the condemned prisoner is only 26 years of age and that he was in love with deceased Dilara which was not returned by her and resisted by her parents and as such death sentence is not called for in the facts of the present case.

<u>18. We have given our anxious consideration to this material aspect as because the life of a young man is involved in this case. Had it been an admitted or convincingly established case of a jilted lover then probably we could have given some consideration to the question of sentence in the facts of the case. But from the evidence it only transpired that the condemned prisoner used to tease deceased Dilara and her sister Mina while they used to go to school. It is also on record that he gave a proposal of marriage with deceased Dilara and the same was rejected by the deceased and her parents. There is nothing on record either from the prosecution side or from the defence side to show that there was (any real) love between the appellant and deceased Dilara. Hence, the appellant being not a jilted lover, we find it really difficult to commute the sentence of death to one of imprisonment for life. Further, soon before the occurrence there was no provocation from the prosecution side and there was no occasion for the appellant to show any emotional imbalance and disequilibrium. On the contrary, the evidence on record shows that the appellant in a premeditated and pre-planned manner entered into the but of the deceased with a dagger and killed her. In the case of Abed Ali (Condemned prisoner) Vs. The State, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 171, we have considered as to what constitutes extenuating circumstances and we have further held in that decision that in the facts of each particular case the extenuating circumstances are to be judicially determined. The trial Court as also the High Court Division found no mitigating circumstances. Nor did we. Thus, considering all aspects of the case and keeping in view the question of sentence, we find it very difficult to reduce the sentence of death to the lesser sentence of imprisonment for life.</u>

Accordingly, the appeal and the jail petition are dismissed.

End.
